commentary.title: Recap of eventful Qatar Grand Prix second practice
summary: Leclerc spins; Gasly causes red flag after spin
Hamilton stops on track after loss of power
Antonelli tops first practice; Russell 2nd; Hadjar 3rd
Qatar first of two races set to end F1 season despite unrest in Middle East
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli already crowned champion

posts.title: Mercedes set pace in disrupted second practice in Qatar
text: World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix.
Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session.
Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid.

The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes.
The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin.
Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs.
The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions.

text: That is all from us today. Thank you for your company.
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli has been the fastest driver in both practice sessions on Friday.
George Russell has been second in both sessions too, can the Mercedes keep up their form?
We will be back tomorrow to take you through FP3 and qualifying, from 14:15 GMT.
Lights out for FP3 at 14:30.

Enjoy the rest of your evening and we will see you tomorrow.
Take care.

posts.title: Get Involved - tension at Ferrari
text: Rob: Hamilton and Leclerc should sit out alternate races until the end of the season. That would maximise results for Ferrari and each driver.
Andrew: Ferrari needs to get rid of Leclerc and give Lewis a teammate who will work with him and not against him. Leclerc is like Verstappen a selfish driver who is not a team player.

Jen: Think Charles feels threatened for the first time.
Plus as the golden boy Champion in waiting !! How many years more does he need !! 8 years plenty

posts.title: Chequered flag
text: Second practice has come to an end.
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli continues to be the fastest driver out on track, after also being fastest in the first session.
His team-mate George Russell is second and Lando Norris, in the McLaren, is third.
Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen make up the top five.
A minute left of this session. It has been a busy one.
Time for drivers to get in one more lap.
Virtual safety car has been deployed as Lewis Hamilton gets out of the Ferrari and makes his way off the circuit.

posts.title: Yellow flag
text: Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari has gone off the track and stopped.
"Something's happened, I've lost power," Hamilton said on the radio.
"I've lost the engine," he added.
McLaren's Oscar Piastri gets a little too close with Franco Colapinto's Alpine but they get away cleanly.
The pair have a train going on with Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes behind them.
Drivers are getting on with some race runs before the session comes to an end.
Guess who is back in the pits? Pierre Gasly. He's having a look at the data with the Alpine engineers.
10 minutes to go of the extended FP2 session.
Pierre Gasly's Alpine has been rolled back into the garage.
Pierre had gone back into the Alpine motorhome as soon as he thought his session was over.
The two Ferraris and Aston Martins are the only cars in the pits at the moment, everyone else is out on the track.
No further investigation for the Verstappen and Hamilton incident.

Max Verstappen runs a little wide and has a moment with the gravel.
Liam Lawson has a snap of oversteer but keeps control of the car.
Meanwhile, the FIA have noted Lewis Hamilton for driving erratically during that incident with Max Verstappen a little earlier.
After those two red flags, the session has been extended by 13 minutes.
We have 20 minutes to go.

Lewis Hamilton looked like he was on a fast lap when he got into traffic with Max Verstappen, who seemed to be on a long run. Verstappen was on the radio to say the move was under braking - he was not too pleased with that.
Looks like all 21 cars are out on track now after Pierre Gasly's spin.
Time to get in laps before the session ends.
The cars have all lined up in the pit lane as they get ready to head out again.
Before the red flag was waved, Kimi Antonelli was on track for a fast lap. He went purple in sector one but had to back off in sector two when the flag was waved.
